answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new identity to post a refundable bond into a shared crystal escrow. An established peer must bridge the entrant by locking an equal opal-denominated bond of their own. Both unlock only after eight consecutive epochs of unique graded work. Detection of any clone in the bonded set jointly slashes the entire cluster. Each fake therefore demands fresh external capital at risk from a real peer plus the wait, so farms cannot parallelize the cost.
